objective: Implement a Skill-agnostic TaskContextRuntime that owns task/context lifecycle, source verification, evidence decisions, immutable receipts, and delivery acceptance without transferring lifecycle ownership to Skills or Workers.
mustPreserve: completionDecision and deliveryAcceptance remain independent state axes
ESAutomationRunStatus.Accepted remains a run-admission status and is never projected as completionDecision=accepted
Skills declare semantics and preferences but never own task or context lifecycle
Workers provide execution results and candidate evidence but never self-accept completion
candidate outcome, evidenceHash, and producerType remain non-authoritative inputs; platform-normalized values come only from the verifier selected by the frozen AcceptanceProfile
canonical CandidateEvidence uses the central platform Evidence contract while legacy TaskContext v1 payloads enter only through an explicit compatibility projection
the frozen AcceptanceProfile and accepted Receipt bind the central Evidence contract ID and SHA-256; contract drift limits the current completion claim
every required claim has an explicit registered verifier binding whose declared claim scope, definition hash, and registry snapshot hash are frozen
optional observation claims have explicit registered verifier bindings but never participate in completionDecision, required evidence freshness, or task hard-blocking

human correction observations are derived only by platform rereading a task-bound Codex transcript slice under the trusted session root; candidate counts and whole-session projections are non-authoritative
task transcript bindings contain no transcript text and bind TaskId, GoalRevisionHash, TaskRevision, ContextVersion, SessionId, source prefix hash, exact line range, and normalized slice hash

a transcript-capable TaskContext freezes interactionSessionId at creation, and the verifier accepts only the last non-injected user message before the frozen task creation timestamp plus its first post-creation user follow-up
verifier registry structure and semantics reject duplicate identity, unanchored claim scope, field duplication, unsupported authority expansion, and bound-definition drift
Core v1 integration acceptance distinguishes prohibited capabilities from conditionally selected adapter capabilities
missing conditional adapter capabilities never block StaticReview or EngineeringReadiness

accepted completion requires frozen AcceptanceProfile, complete fresh EvidenceSet, verified sourceScope, no critical contradiction, no unresolved source drift, bounded UnverifiedClaims, and an immutable bound Receipt
every TaskContext binds one immutable frozen GoalRevision by goalId, goalRevision, and goalRevisionHash

every TaskContext binds one platform-verified RoutePlan whose canonical hash, exact routeKeys, stage registry membership, GoalRevision SourceRef, registry SourceRef, Git HEAD, and all SourceRef hashes are independently replayable
PowerShell RoutePlan producers, validators, fixtures, and TaskContext consumers use one shared canonicalization and validation implementation rather than copying the hash algorithm
RoutePlan validation failure limits only the current RoutePlan or completion claim and never projects into project-global P0
GoalRevision is reread and rehashed before accepted completion; Goal drift limits only the current completion claim
all state mutations use TaskRevision and ContextVersion compare-and-swap
allowedTransitions: Completed+Frozen with deliveryAcceptance=pending -> deliveryAcceptance=rejected without rolling back completionDecision
Completed+Frozen -> explicit Reopen -> Active+Live at a new TaskRevision and ContextVersion
Live or Compacting -> PartiallyInvalidated on source drift
PartiallyInvalidated -> Live only after explicit source reverification
non-quarantined context -> Quarantined -> compatible recovered context
forbiddenTransitions: accepted completion with missing or stale required evidence
accepted completion without a verified sourceScope binding
accepted completion after central Evidence contract drift or with an EvidenceSet bound to another contract hash
optional observation absence, staleness, or verifier failure -> task completion blocked
whole-session correction count -> arbitrary task-object humanCorrectionRate
candidate-provided correction count -> platform correction observation
system, developer, world-state, or reasoning content -> persisted task transcript slice
receipt mutation or acceptance of an orphan receipt
state mutation with stale TaskRevision or ContextVersion
Skill or Worker directly changing lifecycle state outside the platform API
substitution of Automation run Accepted for TaskContextRuntime completion accepted
global Skill auto-wrapping or discovery-triggered automatic business execution
requiring an unselected adapter capability for StaticReview or EngineeringReadiness
creating a TaskContext from a RoutePlan whose selected stage is not registered for the exact profile and at least one frozen routeKey
creating a TaskContext from a RoutePlan whose GoalRevision or route-stage registry is absent from the canonical SourceRef set
accepting a depth-2 stage without an exact directional registry authorization for the frozen profile and routeKey
acceptanceSignals: the central Evidence schema validates canonical, legacy compatibility, and normalized records while TaskContext schema references the normalized definition instead of copying it
the verifier registry schema and semantic validator pass definition-drift and unrelated-registry-addition counterexamples
optional verifier bindings are frozen, validated, and replayed without changing the required-claim completion decision
task transcript slice tests reject wrong TaskId, GoalRevisionHash, revision/version, SessionId, source prefix hash, truncated range, cross-task reuse, and whole-session projection
verified task transcript slices derive correction observations without persisting transcript text, while missing bindings keep humanCorrectionRate evidence-pending/null

deterministic static tests pass accepted, rejected, undetermined, delivery independence, illegal transition, CAS conflict, idempotency, drift, receipt tamper, orphan receipt, reopen, path escape, and interruption recovery cases
Skill discovery and route validators find exactly one TaskContextRuntime Skill
integration policy validation proves stable capability identities and profile isolation
strict UTF-8 and target diff checks pass
RoutePlan contract tests recompute routePlanHash, routePlanId, sourceRefsHash, Git HEAD, GoalRevision binding, registry binding, stage membership, and depth authorization from real fixture artifacts

forged RoutePlan hash, forged SourceRef hash, missing GoalRevision SourceRef, missing registry SourceRef, unregistered stage, profile mismatch, routeKey mismatch, and unauthorized depth are rejected before TaskContext creation
counterexamples: A worker returns success and the task becomes Completed without platform evidence evaluation
A user rejects delivery and the historical completion receipt is deleted or downgraded
A stale caller overwrites a newer context revision
A ReadSnapshot source changes after evidence capture but accepted completion still succeeds
a TaskContext is created without a frozen GoalRevision or with a forged GoalRevision hash
a generic source hash verifier is used to prove compilation, Runtime, Release, performance, visual, or arbitrary domain success
a GoalRevision changes after task creation but completion still issues an accepted Receipt
a producer adds an authority-like field or forges the central Evidence contract hash and the platform accepts it
an optional interaction observation is absent and completion becomes undetermined or rejected
a candidate chooses a shorter transcript range that omits a correction and the platform accepts the claimed normalized slice hash
a transcript slice for another TaskId or GoalRevision is reused in the current task
a whole Codex session correction count is assigned to one TaskContext without an exact line-range binding
system or developer messages are copied into a project artifact or metric report
An immutable receipt exists without a committed event and is treated as authoritative
StaticReview fails because AIBrain runTask, ESAutomationFacade, Worker, Codex Session, Semantic Archive, or Unity Editor integration is absent
a correctly hashed RoutePlan with an unregistered stage, mismatched routeKey, or forged snapshot is accepted because only JSON Schema shape was checked
the RoutePlan validator and TaskContext consumer implement different canonical field sets and therefore disagree on the same immutable artifact
nonGoals: automatic wrapping of all Skills in TaskContextRuntime
unselected AIBrain, ESAutomationFacade, Worker, Codex Session, Semantic Archive, or Unity Editor adapters
rewriting existing Skills to own TaskContextRuntime lifecycle
treating deliveryAcceptance=pending as failure after accepted platform completion
Unity Runtime, Worker Runtime, release, Git, history, or audit-state execution
assumptions: PowerShell 5.1 or later is available for the platform-neutral static core
project-relative source paths are the only accepted sourceScope path form
create-only event snapshots are sufficient for v1 recovery and auditability
sourceRefs: current user transcript: fixed TaskStatus/ContextStatus and completion/delivery semantics
priorContradictions: Revision 1 left integration capability profile isolation implicit, which could let a future validator misclassify optional adapter gaps as Core v1 acceptance failures.
Revision 2 did not freeze verifier definition identity or constrain which claim kind a verifier could prove, and did not revalidate GoalRevision at completion.
Revision 3 still embedded Evidence input/output structure in TaskContextRuntime and did not freeze a central Evidence contract identity.

Revision 4 bound RoutePlan hashes and SourceRefs but did not freeze routeKeys or require the consumer to replay exact stage/Profile/route/depth registry membership through one shared canonical implementation.
Revision 5 left optional observability claims implicit and therefore could either block completion or tempt a caller to project whole-session correction counts into an arbitrary task.

Revision 6 compared candidate transcript fields to Task identity but did not freeze the Codex session or task-creation time anchor, leaving same-format cross-session or pre-task slice substitution possible.

recovery.resumeAction: Load and verify the last contiguous valid event chain; ignore unreferenced orphan receipts; retry with the current TaskRevision and ContextVersion.
recovery.partialStatePolicy: Fail closed on event gaps, hash mismatch, invalid transition, receipt mismatch, or source drift; never overwrite an existing event or receipt.
